Five Apple Watch models can measure your blood pressure and alert you to possible high blood pressure, but they won't give you an actual reading.

Some smart rings and other fitness devices can do this, but require periodic calibration with a traditional cuff blood pressure monitor. The upcoming Signal Ring claims to provide full blood pressure readings without any calibration, backed by clinical trials involving thousands of people…

「Silent Killer」

Abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension) and abnormally low blood pressure (hypotension) can both pose significant health risks.

Of the two, high blood pressure is more dangerous, hence known as the 「silent killer,」 because it can cause serious and irreversible damage to your arteries, heart, and brain without obvious symptoms. The condition often goes undetected until it triggers a heart attack or stroke.

For seniors, regular blood pressure monitoring is especially important, and home cuff-type blood pressure monitors are available on the market. However, being able to monitor automatically through a fitness device you already wear would certainly be the ideal approach.

Apple Watch blood pressure features

The launch of watchOS 26 has enabled five Apple Watch models to measure blood pressure:

  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2

However, these models won't give you any readings, but will alert you when possible signs of high blood pressure are detected. Other devices such as the Oura Ring work in a similar way.

Some fitness devices can indeed provide actual blood pressure readings, but they require regular calibration with readings from a cuff blood pressure monitor.

Signal Ring

Startup company Vital Signals has announced it has developed a smart ring, the Signal Ring, which claims to achieve measurement accuracy comparable to a traditional arm cuff blood pressure monitor without any calibration required.

According to Bloomberg, CEO Tom Moss said he nearly died from an undiagnosed case of high blood pressure before founding the company.

The ring begins pre-ordering later today, ships in October, and is priced at US$399 with no subscription required. Real-time blood pressure readings and long-term tracking data can be displayed on the accompanying app (see image above).

It is worth noting that the Oura Ring has not yet been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), but clinical trials have shown that it can provide accurate blood pressure readings for thousands of participants.

Interestingly, Moss has no intention of selling this ring to everyone. He says these professional features are most suitable for seniors and people assessed by doctors as being at risk for high blood pressure, implicitly suggesting that the Signal Ring may not excel in other areas (such as sleep tracking).
